@graph.name: Search Index Supply & Standing Operations
@graph.description: Search index supply and standing operations for The Flat Rate Movers: the standing measurement system of the Retrieval Machine’s search-index element. One dataset file joins the demand side (the buyer-intent query clusters generated from the estate’s own rubric), the supply side (every page of the estate with its schema types, word count, internal inlinks, per-page JSON digest and indexation state), and the evidence side (sampled standing, Search Console verdicts and the era-tagged pre-rebuild console window), plus the competitor supply observed in the same sampling, the third-party records that corroborate or corrupt the company’s facts, and the named gaps with their designed solutions. Standing is recorded only from evidence that exists: a cluster with no observation carries no standing row, observed absence is recorded as observed absence, and no position, rating or metric is invented or zero-filled anywhere in the file.

@graph.name: Search Index Scope and Footprint
@graph.description: The scope the standing system measures: 308 pages in the registry, 34 published services, and the 87-feature service-area footprint (Winchester footprint 60 areas, Martinsburg footprint 48 areas, 21 shared). The two branches are distinct in every table of this file: Winchester is The Flat Rate Movers (116 W Piccadilly St Suite 11, Winchester, VA 22601; hours Mon-Fri 8-6, Sat 8-4, Sun 9-4; Google rating 5.0 from 2 reviews) and Martinsburg is Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV (736 Williamsport Pike Suite 2, Martinsburg, WV 25404; hours Mon-Fri 9-6, Sat 9-4, Sun 9-4; Google rating 4.7 from 6 reviews). Branch facts are never blended.

@graph.name: Search Index Taxonomy
@graph.description: The vocabularies every table in this file uses. Intent classes: the rubric’s five generated classes (ai-question, best-choice, cost, how-process, navigational-local) plus sampled-money-query for the observation-defined clusters. Geo scopes: pattern-family (area-null rows: near-me and national pattern forms), the branch scopes (scope-winchester, scope-martinsburg, scope-shenandoah-valley), town scopes (place-*), corridor scopes (i-81, i-66, i-70), and the sampled state and port scopes. Observation methods: serp-sample, places-sample, gsc-inspection, gsc-export, bing-wmt and prompt-panel (the last two have no observations yet and are named so future rows keep their own method rather than borrowing one). Eras: pre-rebuild (console windows predating the rebuilt site), transition (the console window spanning the rebuild) and post-rebuild. Indexation states: indexed, not-indexed, unobserved. Third-party record statuses: open, correction sent, corrected-live, parked-owner-step.

@graph.name: Query Clusters
@graph.description: The demand side: 15856 query clusters grouping all 42471 intent-rubric rows by service, intent class, geo scope and target URL. Each cluster carries its canonical query (the shortest variant, the cluster’s representative phrasing), every variant phrasing, the rubric row ids it groups, and a money weight: the sampled money clusters carry the owner’s priority classes from the research dossier (P1 B2B and freight money plus the defended gun-safe #1, P2 the Winchester head terms, P3 the Martinsburg defense and category hubs); generated clusters carry "standard", meaning not separately owner-ordered. Cluster derivation is mechanical — no cluster is hand-written, and an observation-defined cluster whose text matches no rubric row carries an empty rubricRowRefs list rather than invented refs.

@graph.name: Search Index Gap Records
@graph.description: The named gaps of the search-index element, 9 records, each with its requirement reference, evidence references, impact, status, resolving batch — and its designed solution. A gap in this file is a work item with a fix attached, never a bare problem statement.

gapRecords.title: Prominence is the binding constraint, not technical supply
gapRecords.requirementRef: Dossier 01 §6 G1 (Claude gates: Corroborated × Worth citing)
gapRecords.impact: Technical supply is at its measured ceiling (verify suite green, Performance 100). Pack order and corroboration decide the head local queries now, and both are built from evidence assets, not from review volume: the company’s high-value and government/military clients do not write reviews, which is a settled fact of this market, not a deficit to engineer around.
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Retrieval Machine B7 (proof-asset cadence) + Dossier 03 corroboration program
gapRecords.solution: Prominence from evidence assets the company controls: the anonymized job-story engine across every industry served, Business Profile completeness and post cadence on the two in-scope profiles, third-party citation accuracy, and machine citation of the datasets through the answer panel. No review solicitation program exists or is planned.

gapRecords.title: Dedicated B2B pages not yet the returned URL (G2 anomaly)
gapRecords.impact: For racking, data-center and medical queries the gun-safe hub is the returned company URL while the dedicated pages stand live and in the sitemap. If the cause is hub-signal concentration rather than indexation lag, the dedicated pages will not take over unaided.
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Retrieval Machine B2 (verdict reconciliation), then B3 only if B2 finds concentration
gapRecords.solution: B2 reconciles the Search Console verdicts against the sampled returns and publishes the determination in this table; B3 (hub-to-dedicated internal-signal consolidation) runs only on a concentration finding. Against lag, the designed response is time plus the standing indexing cadence, not edits.

gapRecords.title: Hub-fragment dependence for transloading and port intent
gapRecords.impact: The hub carries embedded sections for adjacent intents; answer engines cite the fragment while search returns the hub. The dedicated pages must win their own queries outright.
gapRecords.solution: Answer-fragment binding (Dossier 02): each money question gets one canonical fragment on its dedicated page, with the hub fragment demoted to a pointer. Runs inside B3 if B2 confirms concentration.

gapRecords.title: Third-party records still corrupt on money queries
gapRecords.impact: Stale addresses, an invented discount and wrong authority framings circulate on records a searcher or an answer engine can read instead of the company’s own surfaces.
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Retrieval Machine B4 (third-party correction wave; owner steps as one consolidated sitting)
gapRecords.solution: The registry in this dataset generates the owner-step list; corrections run in dependency order (Data Axle root first, then the aggregator-fed records get one refresh cycle before any direct-edit retry). "Corrected-live" is claimed only on direct-fetch proof.

gapRecords.title: No Bing channel at all
gapRecords.impact: No verified Bing Webmaster property, no IndexNow, no Bing Places work: the estate is invisible to the second engine’s consoles and its AI surfaces that draw on the same index.
gapRecords.solution: Verify the Webmaster property through the existing DNS access, publish an IndexNow key file as a new sealed distribution, wire deploy-hook submissions, and import the first Bing standing into this dataset’s observation table under its own method (bing-wmt), never averaged with Google methods.

gapRecords.title: Datasets not present in Google Dataset Search at audit
gapRecords.impact: The 33 dataset files are fully marked up and landed, but the catalog surface that aggregates datasets had not picked them up at audit time.
gapRecords.status: open — routed to the dataset-catalog element
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: Dossier 04 program (re-check on the measurement cadence)
gapRecords.solution: Presence is re-checked on the measurement cadence; the dataset-catalog dossier owns the verdict and any additional registration routes. No markup change is indicated: the Dataset schema is checker-verified every batch.

gapRecords.title: Proof assets are thin for the B2B categories
evidenceRefs: Blog program record (first job story live 2026-10-31)
gapRecords.impact: The categories with the highest contract value have the fewest citable proof assets; the first anonymized job story (a 1,650 lb gun safe delivered and installed in Moorefield, WV) is live, and the pipeline behind it is the fix.
gapRecords.solution: The job-story pipeline runs on the blog program’s gates with client identity never published: one story per completed job the owner clears, told by scope, weight, terrain and method. Cadence, not campaigns.

gapRecords.title: No standing dataset existed (closed by this build)
gapRecords.impact: Before this build, sampled standing lived in prose dossiers and console verdicts lived in a log; neither was a queryable, sealed, regenerating dataset.
gapRecords.status: closed by B1 for the dataset; the prompt panel itself is Dossier 02 A1
gapRecords.solution: This dataset: regenerated from the live estate by scripts/build-search-index.js in the batch cadence, sealed in the signed index, with method-and-era discipline enforced at generation. The remaining instrument gap — citation standing on the answer engines’ own surfaces — is Dossier 02’s Answer Panel, a separate build.

gapRecords.title: Stale pre-rebuild page still in the index, feeding a third-party error
gapRecords.impact: The company’s own stale pre-rebuild page (a free-estimates post from the old site) carries the same invented 15% discount text a third-party record now attributes to the company. Correcting only the third party leaves the source standing.
gapRecords.resolvingBatch: A later retirement batch (sequenced with the correction wave)
gapRecords.solution: Two-sided: retire the stale page from the estate (with its sitemap, registry and seal consequences handled as a normal batch), then re-run the third-party correction with the source gone.

@graph.name: How the Search Index Dataset Is Built
@graph.description: Method. The generator (scripts/build-search-index.js in the Flat Rate Machine) reads the paths registry for every location and builds all seven tables from the live estate in one run: clusters are grouped mechanically from the rubric database by (service, intent class, geo scope, target URL); URL supply is mined from the registries, the source shell, the served head data and the per-page JSON files; standing observations are admitted only from evidence on file — the research dossier’s dated live sampling and the Search Console verdicts — and the generator rejects any observation missing its method, era or source; the console window is joined from the rubric’s era-tagged evidence tables without aggregation or zero-filling; competitor, third-party and gap records are transcribed from the research dossiers with their check dates, under a schema bar the generator enforces in code. The url_supply digest is the SHA-256 of the page’s per-page JSON file in the public tree at generation time; a completed batch seals exactly those bytes, and the verification suite asserts the supply digests equal the served signed index after every batch. The file’s dateModified is the estate lastmod-ledger date for this file’s URL, wired by the seal (Batch Q124, 2026-11-03) — outside a seal the generator falls back to the newest evidence date among its inputs — never the wall clock, so regeneration is byte-stable and checkable. Update cadence: the dataset regenerates in every estate batch that changes pages, rubric rows or standing evidence, and reseals in the same motion.

@graph.name: Search Index Dataset Sources
@graph.description: Sources, with their dates and eras kept distinct. (1) The estate’s own registries and rubric database — the demand and supply truth, current at generation. (2) Live search sampling of 2026-10-31 (Retrieval Machine Dossier 01 §§2–3): sampled positions and pack orders, labeled [OBS] in the dossier, post-rebuild era, small-sample by design and never blended with console data. (3) Search Console URL-inspection verdicts of 2026-10-31: 11 URLs inspected in the standing indexing pass; the same verdicts were ingested into the rubric outcome-evidence log (161 evidence rows). (4) The Search Console performance export for 2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28: pre-rebuild era evidence, attached to rubric rows by exact normalized text match only where the target page existed in the export and still exists; its totals describe the old site, not this one. (5) Third-party record checks of 2026-10-30 (backlink program wave 1) and 2026-10-31 (Dossier 03 re-verification, with each crawl’s age stated there). No source is presented as fresher than it is.

@graph.name: Search Index Boundaries and Non-Claims
@graph.description: What this dataset never does. It never invents a position, a metric, a rating or a review count — for the company or for any competitor. It never presents the pre-rebuild console window as current performance, and never averages methods together. It never claims a third-party record corrected without direct-fetch proof. It contains no representation of any service the company has not confirmed and published through the normal estate path: the research dossiers’ expansion candidates (after-hours cross-dock work, auction-exit medical logistics, data-center decommissioning’s physical layer, small-count rack moves as a named segment, equipment buyback) appear nowhere in this file and enter only if the owner confirms the capability and the service is published first. Competitor records are benchmark observations about their owners’ supply and feed no company claim. The provenance certificate proves origin and integrity of this file only; it is not a ranking input and is not represented as one.
